title: Vue performance: measure the expensive boundary
outcome: Find whether a slow interaction comes from work, rendering, layout, or network delay.
useCase: Large ticket tables and optional rich editors.
benefits: Improves the delay users actually experience.
drawbacks: Optimizations can add stale-state, focus, and maintenance costs.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs
cue: Measure one delay. Fix one cause. Retest the task.

trace.title: Slow interaction
trace.detail: Start with a measured symptom: typing takes 200 ms to appear with 5,000 tickets. Profile before choosing a fix. Filtering, component updates, layout, and network work have different repairs.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Record interaction → long task → flame chart → expensive function or layout. Change one thing and compare with the same synthetic dataset/device conditions. Keep a correctness check alongside the timing check.

If the server sends 50,000 rows, frontend tricks may hide a poor data boundary. Consider server filtering, pagination, and bounded responses before rendering every row.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A fast desktop can hide mobile main-thread cost. Virtualization can break screen-reader context. A deep watcher over a large tree may run more work than the user action needs.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Find whether a slow interaction comes from work, rendering, layout, or network delay. Explain one example and one failure.
